newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia could become "economic superpower" - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Russia could become "economic superpower" - IMF.

text.p: IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus said on Thursday that a reformist Russia could become an "economic superpower" but that parliament had a major role to play to ensure conditions were right.

"This country can be an economic superpower, but this cannot be achieved without reforms," Camdessus told the budget committee of the State Duma lower house of parliament. "We believe this is a window of opportunity but the State Duma has an enormous responsibility to create the necessary structure."

Ministers say Russia's new tax code is needed to underpin the budget, but the document is stalled in the Duma, which is dominated by communists and other conservatives. Deputies also delayed the 1997 budget for months, complaining it was unrealistic and did not meet the needs of impoverished Russians.

Camdessus, in Moscow for talks with President Boris Yeltsin and his new government team, said the Duma had to be realistic. "You cannot ruin your own credibility by telling your people you can have a high rate of growth without reform," he said.

He said a 1997 programme being worked out between Russia and the IMF would aim to strengthen central bank control over commercial banks and develop a commercial bank-funded deposit insurance scheme. Russia needed powers to punish those who did not pay their tax and to modernise the tax service.
